blocks.intro: A routine visit stops your water for [routine visit downtime, hours] at most, at a time you choose.

blocks.h: Like for like, or a change?
blocks.intro: Like for like under your procedure keeps the system qualified. A change waits for your change control (EU GMP Annex 15, 11; GUI-0029, 7). Not under GMP: we test a change against your specification.
rows: Operational qualification (OQ) at design recovery; closer sampling

items.q: Will servicing affect our qualified state?
items.a: Not when parts are like for like under your procedure; we supply the input for your change request.

items.q: What does our team do between visits?
items.a: [operator time, minutes a day]: read conductivity and alarms, keep the daily log and top up softener salt. Call at the first odd reading; a fault reported early is shorter to fix. The daily log is also one of your warranty conditions.

items.q: We stop production for two weeks. What does the system need?
items.a: [idle-period rules by duration]; the rules change with how long the system stands. Your operating manual carries the steps. Before the water goes back into use, your restart sampling and release apply. Tell us the dates if you want a visit for the restart.

items.q: Do you service other makers' systems?
items.a: Yes, for [makes and equipment types serviced]. We start with a condition survey and a review of drawings, records and spares, then quote a plan. Missing records do not stop a visit. Parts for other makes: [parts supplied for other makes].

items.q: Will you work to our SOPs and forms?
items.a: Yes, on request: we follow your standard operating procedures (SOPs) and fill in your work orders and logbooks. We take your site induction, and good manufacturing practice (GMP) training where it applies, and work under your permits. Planned visits are booked [planned visit notice, working days] ahead, so permits and induction are ready.
Within [travel time from service base, hours] of anywhere in [service coverage area]. Coverage by province is on our locations page.

items.q: How long are parts available for a system this age?
items.a: [parts availability period, years] from handover, for every package we build. Pumps, membranes, instruments and valves are makers’ catalogue parts. When a maker retires one, we name the successor and say whether it is like for like or a change.
